intended_object: An internal "residual" hypothesis in the library's proof chain toward AX1 (the asymptotic triangle packing statement). It is the statement that, for all ε, δ > 0, the gap ν₃*(G) − ν₃(G) is at most ε|V|² for all sufficiently large graphs whose vertices are isolated or have degree ≥ δ|V| and which satisfy ν₃*(G) > ε|V|². Source: the docstring and the module docs of CoreGapAX1.lean.
explanation: CoreGapResidual is a Prop-valued intermediate hypothesis, which the module docs call "the residual". It exists only to drive the checked reductions CoreGapResidual → NibbleGapResidual → NibbleGapHyp → AX1Statement, and the file also proves the converse direction. It lives in an `Internal` folder and is a restricted, reformulated case of the Haxell–Rödl theorem (ν₃* − ν₃ = o(n²)), tailored to the proof: the isolated-or-δ|V|-degree condition and the "fractionally rich" assumption ν₃* > ε|V|². It is not a standard notion from the literature. The statement itself is well formed: the quantifiers ∀ε>0 ∀δ>0 ∃n₀ ∀G are correct, and coreGapResidual_of_haxellRodl confirms it is a true special case of Haxell–Rödl. As a mathematical object, however, it is a proof device. Mathlib has no counterpart, since it has no fractional triangle packing or Haxell–Rödl statement.
